derivedFrom: the decision that a claim is a sentence and every sentence in a researched section names the document it rests on, taken with the two decisions it reads, that every number in written prose exists in the facts file and every researched claim names a stored source, and with SCHEMA's statement of the four statuses. Each verdict below was written from those rules and from what each paragraph in research-prose.json says it carries, not from a run of the checker: the poisoned paragraph changes one figure so its refusal names that figure, the unsourced claim adds one sentence with no citation and no digit so only the citation rule can refuse it, and the section with no admissible source cites only refused documents so it falls back before any sentence is read. The facts the figures are matched against are read back from a replayed store at test time and are not stated here.

a poisoned paragraph.reason: a figure the facts file does not hold

an unsourced claim.offending: Analysts expect the next design cycle to be the strongest in five years.

a claim resting on a refused document.reason: a citation to a document admissibility refused

a cause citing a release filed after the.reason: a citation to a document published outside the move it gives the cause of
a cause citing a release filed after the.offending: D1 published 2026-08-18, outside the move ending 2026-02-24 measured from 2026-02-17

a cause naming no move.reason: a cause naming the session of no move the facts file holds
a cause naming no move.offending: Keysight shares moved on record third quarter revenue of $1.85 billion [D1].

note: two rows' worth of reason are kept for a section refused twice, the first attempt's on its own rejected row and the second's on the fallback row, and the run log line for the second check names both. The clean paragraphs are asserted accepted in the same run as the refusals, because a checker that refused everything would satisfy every refusal above and fail only these two.
